claims.claim: The F3 recurrent history-conditioned update replicates in FRESH_V1 and FRESH_V2.
History-specific transformation generalizes from AB/BA to the orthogonal C4 probe and persists through D64.
At least 17 omission-identifiable, future-relevant causal distinctions coexist in the tested bounded worlds while future causal capacity remains observable.
Stages 9-16 reuse the first cycle's 34 event sites and introduce zero new event sites.
Accumulated dose is sufficient for global landscape expansion, while event order determines the exact future organization.
After HOST_STOP, reachability continues to evolve and the temporal transformation differs among H0, AB, and BA; the observed phenomenon is continuous rather than an isolated discrete transition.

The tested P1/P2/P3 instances did not show history-driven equivalence breaking, but FULL-vs-OMIT effects were not future-relevant under the frozen panel, so this is not a general bounded null for equivalent causal opportunities.
Loss-then-recovery renewal was not observed because capacity did not fall in the tested domain.
No acquired organization autonomously generated the next unpreloaded experience.
Formal RW3 and L4 remain unproven.
No new unpreloaded contingency or self-generated next experience was demonstrated after HOST_STOP.
History-conditioned post-HOST_STOP dynamics replicate in MAIN_S0, FRESH_V1, and FRESH_V2 using raw_a and future RAW responses without clock_a in the pass gate.
AB and BA histories break causal equivalence among three initially equivalent, future-relevant opportunities in different persistent ways across MAIN and two fresh transforms.
No prevalidated near-boundary causal configuration was found in the frozen C0/C3/C4 panel; this does not negate native boundary crossings outside the tested panel.
Independent RAW-only and sensitive-opportunity methods converge on history-conditioned native dynamics that reorganize existing causal possibilities after host withdrawal.
